name: seeded-skyline
title: Seeded random skyline
summary: A night city generated from seeded randomness: 14 towers whose heights, window counts and lit windows all come from seed(n, rand()) keyed on the loop indices, under 50 seeded stars; identical on every render.
prompt: Generate a night skyline: a row of towers of random heights with randomly lit windows, a moon and stars, the same picture every time.
teaches: Get a repeatable random number per item with seed(key, rand()): it reseeds the generator with key, then evaluates rand()
Recompute the same seeded value wherever it is needed (tower top, window rows, window y) instead of storing it: the same key always gives the same number
Combine nested loop indices into one key (i * 389 + j * 41 + k * 7 + 20000) for a value per window, and threshold it with step(…, 0.55) for on/off
Use seeded values in a loop's until: floor((40 + 110 * seed(…)) / 10) − 1 window rows per tower
pitfalls: Consecutive small seeds (i + 1) give first values that rise or fall in a ramp, because the seed is the float's bits: spread the keys with a multiplier (i * 97 + 3) and give x, y and size different multipliers or the stars fall on a line
rand() without seed() is different on every evaluation and every load; the C++ renderer needs --seed to pin it
A variable holding seed(…) is not a stored number but an expression; inside a loop write the seed inline with the loop index

A seeded scene drawn for a 360×200 box leaves a blank strip in a wider host: drive the loop count from componentWidth() and stand the towers on componentHeight(); since each tower is keyed by its index, the ones that were there keep their look

snippets.note: tower top: @h - 40 - 110 * seed(i * 97 + 3, rand()), standing on the live bottom edge
window rows from the same seeded height
lit or dark: 0.9 * step(seed(window key, rand()), 0.55)
50 stars with separate keys for x, y, size and brightness

check.describe: Fourteen dark towers of mixed heights with scattered amber windows, a pale moon top right and faint stars; the picture is the same on every render. Resized, the sky fills the box and the towers stand on its bottom edge: 9 towers at 234 wide, 21 at 540 (the loop runs to ceil(componentWidth() / 26)); the first towers keep their seeded heights and windows at any size, and the moon stays 60 px from the right.
